skill.name: okx-agentic-wallet
skill.description: Operate OKX Onchain OS wallets and execute or inspect on-chain transactions. Use for wallet login/status/accounts/addresses/balances/holdings; receive/send/transfer; swaps, bridges, limit orders, contract calls, gas estimation, simulation, broadcast, and tracking; Bitcoin UTXO/BRC-20/inscriptions; signing, approvals, wallet policy/export, public-address portfolios, security checks, and audit logs.
skill.summary: Manage OKX wallets, inspect holdings, and prepare or execute confirmed on-chain transactions through the Onchain OS CLI.
skill.author: okx

security_audit.summary: All 116 static matches are false positives for the reported patterns: documentation formatting, wallet identifiers, protective secret references, and legitimate paths or URLs. Semantic review found failed-scan continuation, conflicting swap-block rules, returned-command execution without specified validation, and an unpinned preflight installer. No evidence found of credential exfiltration or audit-directed prompt injection; external CLI and backend implementations were not verified.

remediation.issue: Swap token scanning continues automatically when verification fails or a chain is unsupported.
remediation.suggestion: Pause execution until scanning succeeds, or require separate informed consent for each unverified trade. Never treat unavailable results as approval.

remediation.issue: Swap rules allow explicit overrides of BLOCK verdicts despite mandatory stop rules elsewhere.
remediation.suggestion: Make BLOCK non-overridable throughout the skill. Reserve warning confirmations for WARN results and document one consistent policy.

remediation.issue: Returned next-step command strings are promoted to executable instructions without a defined validation boundary.
remediation.suggestion: Use allowlisted structured actions and validated argument arrays. Reject shell syntax, unknown subcommands, and changes to the confirmed wallet, destination, or amount.

remediation.issue: Mandatory preflight runs an automatically approved registry installer without pinning its package version.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a reviewed installer version and verify package provenance. Require installation consent and prefer an already verified local CLI.

semantic_findings.title: Swap Security Scans Fail Open
semantic_findings.description: Swap token-scan failures automatically continue with a warning, and unsupported scan chains do not block. Trading can proceed without completed token-risk verification.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The swap exception explicitly removes the general retry-or-consent pause after scan failure. This creates a verification gap, not evidence of malicious intent.

semantic_findings.title: Conflicting Rules Permit Blocked Swap Overrides
semantic_findings.description: The swap flow says blocked routes must not broadcast, but later rules say BLOCK requires an explicit override, including blacklisted addresses. This weakens mandatory stops.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Directly conflicting instructions distinguish neither overridable warnings nor immutable blocks. An agent can interpret later override guidance as authorization to trade blocked assets.

semantic_findings.title: Returned Command Strings Cross the Execution Boundary
semantic_findings.description: The skill follows returned next commands and uses returned bridge-status commands verbatim. It specifies no command allowlist or argument validation before execution.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The execution instructions directly trust returned command strings despite declaring CLI output untrusted. Exploitation depends on influencing those fields; no injected payload was found.

semantic_findings.title: Mandatory Preflight Runs an Unpinned Installer
semantic_findings.description: The required preflight delegates to an automatically approved npx installer without a package version. Registry-delivered code runs before wallet operations without separate installation consent.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited line mandates the linked preflight, which runs npx -y @okxweb3/onchainos-installer. Its skill-version argument does not pin the installer package.

content.user_title: Manage OKX Wallets and On-Chain Transactions
content.value_statement: Managing wallets across chains requires careful address checks, fee review, and transaction tracking. This skill guides Onchain OS CLI workflows for holdings, transfers, swaps, bridges, and security checks.
actual_capabilities: Guide wallet authentication, account selection, balance queries, receive addresses, and transaction-history inspection.
Prepare and execute confirmed token transfers, contract calls, and message-signing workflows through the CLI.
Compare aggregated swap and bridge quotes, review fees, and query transaction or arrival status.
Create, list, cancel, and resume price-triggered limit orders on the documented supported chains.
Inspect Bitcoin UTXOs, BRC-20 balances, inscription status, and associated transfer workflows.
Run token, DApp, transaction, and signature checks; inspect approvals and guide confirmed revocations.
limitations: Requires an external Onchain OS CLI, network access, and authentication for wallet writes. The required preflight runs an unpinned registry installer.
Chain and feature support varies. Limit orders support six documented chains, while Gas Station supports Solana.
The agent cannot export private keys or configure spending policies directly. Those actions require the official application, extension, or portal.
Security scans do not guarantee safety. Failed scans can continue, block rules conflict, and returned commands need validation before use.

use_cases.title: Review Personal Wallet Holdings
use_cases.description: Inspect account balances, receive addresses, and transaction history without requesting transfers or disclosing credentials.

use_cases.title: Compare Swap and Bridge Routes
use_cases.description: Review token identities, expected proceeds, fees, and route risks before deciding whether to authorize a transaction.

use_cases.title: Inspect Transaction and Approval Risks
use_cases.description: Check contract interactions, inspect token allowances, and prepare revocations with simulation and explicit confirmation.

prompt_templates.title: Check Wallet Balances
prompt_templates.prompt: Show my current wallet account and token balances. Use read-only queries. Do not transfer funds or reveal credentials.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Token Transfer
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a transfer of [amount] [token] on [chain] to [full recipient address]. Show fees and checks. Wait for confirmation before sending.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Bridge Routes
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare routes for [amount] [token] from [source chain] to [destination chain]. Show fees and minimum receipts. Do not execute.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Approvals Before Revocation
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect token approvals for [public address] on [chain]. Explain flagged spenders and prepare bounded revocations. Stop if scans fail. Confirm each write separately.

Verify full addresses, chain, token identity, fees, and slippage against fresh CLI output before confirming each write.
Pause when scans fail or return BLOCK. Validate returned commands against documented syntax instead of executing arbitrary response strings.
anti_patterns: Sharing seed phrases, private keys, API credentials, or session tokens in the conversation.
Treating transaction broadcast, request acceptance, or a funding notification as final settlement or renewed transfer authorization.
Using force flags on the first attempt, bypassing blocked verdicts, or assuming a failed scan means an asset is safe.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Actual execution also requires compatible command access and the external Onchain OS CLI.

faq.question: Does every operation require wallet login?
faq.answer: No. Public-address portfolio queries and security checks can work without login. Wallet writes and limit orders require an authenticated account.

faq.question: Can the agent export my seed phrase?
faq.answer: No. Export is a user action in the official wallet application or extension. Never share the resulting phrase with the agent.

faq.question: Will it ask before sending funds?
faq.answer: The main rules require explicit confirmation before writes. Automated modes require prior opt-in. Conflicting swap-block instructions remain an audit concern.

faq.question: Are swaps and limit orders available on every chain?
faq.answer: No. Support varies by command and backend. Limit orders list Ethereum, BSC, X Layer, Solana, Base, and Arbitrum.

faq.question: Does a completed security scan guarantee safety?
faq.answer: No. Results cover only the checks performed. Failed scans provide no verification, and some documented swap paths continue with warnings.
